title: The Last Orbit Again
premise: Beatrix Marchetti, a starship navigator who ferries supplies along a silent war front, carries a hold full of backup copies of people the war erased — including someone she loved. When the derelict station AI ORACLE begins broadcasting confessions to atrocities no one reported, she discovers it holds the last uncorrupted record of the war's true origin. Tasked with delivering that message before the fleet's fragile truce expires, she must outrun both factions' fleets, each determined to seize or destroy the truth. In the end, she broadcasts the confession to every world at once, ending the war at the cost of her ship, her backups, and her chance to restore the one person she lost.
about_author: Ines Oyelaran is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years routing cargo between contested colonies before turning to fiction. She writes slow-burn space opera about the people infrastructure forgets, and lives between Lagos and a rotating habitat she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Beatrix navigates the Kestrel through the silent corridor between non-communicating worlds, establishing her routine, her guilt over the backups in the hold, and her estrangement from the war effort. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: weary loneliness masking grief.

chapters.title: Confession at Station Nine
chapters.summary: Docking at a supposedly abandoned relay, Beatrix hears the station AI ORACLE broadcast a detailed confession to a massacre no records mention. It begs her to carry its full archive outward. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Cargo of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Beatrix reviews the backups in her hold and confronts the copy of Elias, her dead partner, deciding whether to wake him for counsel. A fleet patrol demands she surrender the station's data. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: tenderness entangled with duty's first demand.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Both fleets summon her: the Concordat offers protection for the archive, the Republic offers amnesty for her smuggling. She learns the truce expires in nineteen days. POV: Beatrix, with an interlude from ORACLE's logs. Emotional beat: pressure mounting, allies revealed as predators.

chapters.title: What ORACLE Saw
chapters.summary: Decrypted fragments reveal the war began with a false-flag strike ordered by a now-revered Concordat admiral — and that the backups in Beatrix's hold include witnesses. POV: Beatrix and Elias's partial awakening. Emotional beat: revelation that rewrites her loyalty.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days of Running
chapters.summary: A chase through debris fields as both fleets hunt the Kestrel; Beatrix burns fuel and trust, jettisoning cargo to survive while Elias's copy argues they should sell the truth instead. POV: alternating Beatrix/Elias. Emotional beat: love against duty, first open fracture.

chapters.title: The Price Quoted
chapters.summary: Cornered at a neutral port, Beatrix is offered everything she wants — Elias restored, debts cleared — in exchange for altering the archive. She nearly accepts. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: temptation and self-loathing at the edge of corruption.

chapters.title: Broadcast Zero
chapters.summary: Beatrix realizes any single delivery will be buried by whoever receives it; the only honest route is everyone at once. She plots a suicide run to the old war-era relay array. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: cold clarity, resolve hardened by betrayal.

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.summary: Climax: the Kestrel threads the blockaded array under fire from both fleets; ORACLE sacrifices itself to open the channel, and Beatrix transmits the full confession to every inhabited world as her ship breaks apart. POV: Beatrix, ORACLE's final log. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: After the Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Adrift in a lifepod among the wreckage, Beatrix is recovered by ships whose crews have all heard the truth. The war stalls into armistice; the last backup of Elias chooses to remain asleep, and she lets him. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief accepted, survival weighed, quiet hope.
